channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: 8th Annual Print Portfolio Exchange · Rosewood Arts Center
item.description: Rosewood Arts Center, the City of Kettering's arts facility just outside Dayton, Ohio, runs its 8th Annual Print Portfolio Exchange. Participants submit an edition of ten original prints and receive back a random assortment of eight original prints by other participants, plus a commemorative print made by artists at Rosewood and a booklet featuring all of the submitted prints. Of the ten prints submitted, one becomes part of Rosewood's permanent collection and one is exhibited in the Community Gallery as part of the centre's Holiday Sale and fundraiser. The call is open to all artists working in the print medium and any archival print process is acceptable - the centre's own account of the 6th Annual exchange describes a portfolio of relief, intaglio and photographic prints. Paper must measure 5 x 7 inches; prints at any other size are not eligible for the exchange. The edition must be ten identical prints, each signed, dated and numbered 1/10 to 10/10, interleaved with recycled paper, tissue paper or glassine before shipping, with titles optional and contact details welcome on the reverse. Entry is $15, or $10 for students, paid by cheque made out to the City of Kettering or by card over the phone, and the portfolio is posted to Rosewood in Kettering; Dayton-area artists may hand-deliver safely packed work. Entries postmarked by November 7, 2026 will be accepted, and the assembled portfolios are shipped to their new owners by December 15, 2026. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $15 ($10 students). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Revoke Exhibition Open Call
item.description: Revoke Photo Collective's exhibition open call is built around the word REVOKE - revocation as an act of creation, in which something is dismantled so something else can emerge. The brief invites resistance, rebellion, transformation, anger, liberation, rupture, memory, desire and reinvention, with no restrictions on interpretation; the collective says it wants personal and unexpected responses to the word. Open to artists working with photography anywhere, up to 15 images per entry. Selected works are curated by Linda Zhengova, a Czech-Chinese photographer, curator and writer whose own practice deals with representation, sexuality and trauma, into a punk exhibition in Melbourne running October 30 - November 1, 2026. The collective states plainly that this is a curated exhibition and that paying the fee does not guarantee a place in the show. Fees cover venue hire, professional printing, exhibition production and general running costs, so there is no further charge if selected - the collective prints the work and asks selected artists for high-resolution files at that point. Entry runs from A$40 for a single image to A$125 for fifteen. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: A$40–A$125 by image count. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: TRAVEL: Around the World 2026 · Grid Photo Gallery
item.description: International call from Grid Photo Gallery for travel photography in its widest sense - distant landscapes, dense cities, remote territories, familiar streets, cultural spaces, routes, borders, interiors, and environments shaped by movement or belonging. The theme is not limited to the act of travelling: the gallery asks for photographs that open a passage into the world and allow others to enter it through the image, conveying a strong sense of place through visual clarity, composition, atmosphere and intention. Expansive views and intimate details, iconic destinations and overlooked corners, everyday life and extreme or inhospitable environments are all welcome. Selected works are presented in a curated global online exhibition. First place is named Photographer of the Month with a profile interview, priority placement on promotional banners and posters, and a free entry in the next open call; second and third places are highlighted in the virtual exhibition. All selected entries get at least a month on the main-page exhibition and permanent online display afterwards, social media promotion, a digital certificate and a profile page linking to the photographer's website, and the top three become eligible for the Photography of the Year title. Selected works may also appear in a printed catalogue offered for sale. Entries opened September 1 and winners are announced December 1, 2026. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: €7. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Altered Climate — Artdoc Magazine Open Call · Artdoc Photography Magazine
item.description: International open call on global warming, environmental disruption, extreme weather and ecological change. Artdoc invites documentary and art photography alongside altered, abstract, experimental and constructed work, and explicitly encourages images that move beyond literal representation — translating the physical and psychological experience of environmental change through colour, distortion, fragmentation, layering or other photographic intervention. Selected work may be shown in a curated online exhibition, on the Featured Submissions page, or in an upcoming issue of the magazine, with a possible invitation to a portfolio interview. Submissions are free for Artdoc members; non-members must subscribe to reach the form. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication / online exhibition.

item.title: Leighton Artist Studio Residency: Photography 27/28 · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: Self-directed residency of two to six weeks with private use of The Crich Photography Studio — a black-and-white analogue darkroom plus a digital photography setup, in a private studio with mountain views. Best suited to black-and-white film development, processing and printing, digital photography, and some alternative processes including cyanotype; there is no colour darkroom, no digital printing access and no production or technical support, and residents bring their own materials and equipment. Applicants choose preferred dates from three windows between April 5, 2027 and March 31, 2028. Open to individual creative professionals aged 18+ with a demonstrated record, a clearly defined project and proven analogue darkroom experience; domestic and international applicants welcome. Artists who attended any Leighton Studio residency in the past three years are ineligible. The Banff Centre Arts Scholarship covers tuition plus a contribution toward accommodation and meals; Canadian Indigenous applicants receive full tuition, accommodation and meals. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: CAD $65 application fee (CAD $35 for Indigenous applicants); participant cost approx. CAD $1,001.39 per week after the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Visual Arts — Sounding Like a Mountain · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: Five-week faculty-led thematic visual-arts residency (May 17 – June 18, 2027) built around acoustic ecology: how places sing, how memory persists in vibration, and how listening to the land can re-orient ethical and political relations. Participants explore how sound activates multiple temporalities shaped by land use, migration, ecological disruption and colonial infrastructures. Artists get individual studios, access to shared production facilities with technical staff, one-to-one faculty mentorship and studio visits, workshops and peer critique. Faculty are Xenia Benivolski, Elina Waage Mikalsen and Kathryn Yusoff. The program explicitly caters to artists working in photography alongside ceramics, digital media, painting, drawing, printmaking, papermaking, performance art, sculpture and installation. Open to individual artists or duos at any career stage, 18+, domestic and international; applicants need post-secondary training in visual arts or equivalent recognised experience. All participants receive the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship, which covers tuition plus a contribution toward accommodation and meals. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: CAD $65 application fee (CAD $35 for Indigenous applicants); participant cost CAD $4,476.78 after the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Visual Arts — Embodied Making: Performance Art, Images and Objects · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: Five-week faculty-led thematic visual-arts residency (July 5 – August 6, 2027) asking artists to think expansively about performance — how it emerges through movement, stillness, reading, listening, endurance, care and collective action — and how performance and materiality intersect, with images and forms activated and transformed through embodied interaction. Banff's landscape is treated as a collaborator, opening site-responsive and place-based work. Artists get individual studios, shared production facilities with technical staff, one-to-one faculty mentorship and studio visits, workshops and peer critique. Lead faculty are Brendan Fernandes and Claire Fleming Staples, both there for the full five weeks, with Abril Zales (Chief Curator, Museo Tamayo) joining as guest faculty July 12-23. The program explicitly caters to artists working in photography alongside ceramics, digital media, painting, drawing, printmaking, papermaking, performance art, sculpture and installation. Open to individual artists or duos at any career stage, 18+, domestic and international; applicants need post-secondary training in visual arts or equivalent recognised experience. All participants receive the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship, which covers tuition plus a contribution toward accommodation and meals. — Deadline: February 17, 2027. Fee: CAD $65 application fee (CAD $35 for Indigenous applicants); participant cost CAD $4,476.78 after the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Reflections · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: Artspiration Frederick's first cash-and-carry exhibition, on view in the Artspiration Gallery in Frederick, Maryland from 4–20 December 2026. Artists are invited to explore the theme of reflection in nature, in memory, in the self, or in the world around us. Original work in any visual medium is welcome and photography is named outright alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art, with the show seeking a diverse range of artistic voices, perspectives, techniques and subject matter. Open to visual artists 18 and older residing in the continental US; up to three pieces may be submitted and all three may be selected, and work must not have been previously exhibited at Artspiration Frederick. All work must be for sale and the gallery retains 40 percent of a sale, with two-dimensional work framed and wired for hanging (no sawtooth hangers). Accepted work is dropped off 29 November to 1 December, or shipped to arrive by 30 November at the artist's cost with a return label included. The juror's notification is emailed 19 November and the artists' reception is 12 December, 3–5pm. The gallery is free, open to the public and accessible. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: $35 ($25 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Emerging Perspectives Exhibition · The Delaplaine Arts Center
item.description: The Delaplaine Arts Center's annual juried exhibition for young adult artists aged 18 to 35, created around 2021 after the centre noticed a gap in participation from that age group, and open nationally. There are no theme, size or media requirements or restrictions, and photography has shown here before - the 2026 line-up included a silver gelatin print. Work must be original in design and personal execution, made within the past two years and not previously displayed at the Delaplaine; no commercially made prints, giclees or reproductions are considered. The Delaplaine's exhibition-wide AI guidelines apply: work that is solely AI-generated is not considered, AI-assisted work is eligible where the artist's input clearly dominates, and any use of AI must be fully disclosed. Judging runs in two rounds - a remote first round through the online portal that decides acceptance, then in-person judging for the Grand Prize after installation - with the People's Choice decided by visitor ballot through the run of the show. The 2027 juror is Sarah Hempel Irani, a Frederick sculptor working in clay, bronze and stone who teaches sculpture at Frederick Community College and made the Claire McCardell statue on Carroll Creek. Awards are $500 for first place and $250 for the People's Choice. Up to three works may be entered; accepted artwork is delivered 22–28 March 2027 and the exhibition runs 3–25 April 2027, with the juror's talk and award announcement on 3 April. Wall-hanging work need not be framed but must be wired to a professional standard (no sawtooth hangers). Artists are not required to offer work for sale; on a sale the Delaplaine retains 30 percent, or 20 percent for members. — Deadline: February 21, 2027. Fee: $10 ($5 members). Prize: $500 + $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: SAGA Grants 2026 — Round 3 · Spokane Arts
item.description: The Spokane Arts Grant Awards fund arts and culture projects, programs and individual artists in the Spokane region, with requests of any amount up to $10,000 accepted three times a year; Round 3 of the 2026 cycle closes 1 October at 11:59pm and awards are announced 1 December. Spokane Arts will grant $166,000 across 2026 and has made more than a million dollars in awards since 2017. All arts disciplines are encouraged, 'including but not limited to, visual, performing, literary, audio, media arts, humanities, culinary, fashion, architecture, crafts and folk/traditional arts', and a past SAGA grant funded a twelve-page full-colour photographic insert on sixteen African Americans in Spokane for Black Lens News. Individuals apply as a working artist on a solo project - defined as someone trained in a discipline and/or self-identifying as a professional artist - and must hold permanent residency in the Spokane region through the award period; collectives and organisations apply in two separate categories. Applications are free and submitted through SmarterSelect, and each round's portal opens a month before its deadline. Projects must directly impact Spokane; reimbursements for past work, tuition that generates credit, pass-through grants and residency, travel or production costs outside the Spokane area are not funded, and applicants funded in the two previous consecutive years must sit a year out. A selection panel of five to six community members - one city arts commissioner, one Spokane Arts board member and three or four community members with arts experience - weighs artistic merit, effectiveness and community impact; the panel stays anonymous through the granting year, and past rosters are published by year. At least one work sample is required. Spokane Arts also offers one-to-one grant-writing appointments and free information sessions. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $10,000.

item.title: Exploring Muse & Meaning: A Juried Opportunity for Undergraduate Studio Arts Majors · Steffen Thomas Museum of Art
item.description: The Steffen Thomas Museum of Art is a single-artist museum in rural Morgan County, Georgia, built around the work of German-born American painter and sculptor Steffen Thomas, and this is the undergraduate strand of its College Connections programme - the sibling of the MFA-level Truth in Art show it ran earlier in 2026. The point is as much the apprenticeship as the wall space: selected students exhibit at a fine art museum while working alongside museum mentors on curating, loan forms and condition reports, art installation, exhibition promotion and public speaking. Entry is free, and the museum's own call banner limits it to undergraduate studio arts majors in Georgia. Applicants email a bio of up to 250 words, an artist statement of up to 150 words and high-resolution images of three to five works made within the past year, 2D or 3D, each labelled with title, date, dimensions and medium; no piece may exceed 72 x 60 inches or 50 pounds, and artists are responsible for transporting work to and from the museum. The top three Best in Show selections receive $500, $300 and $100. Submissions close 1 November 2026 and the exhibition opens 9 January 2027 at the museum on Bethany Road in Buckhead, about ten minutes from historic Madison. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 / $300 / $100 + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Street Photography Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to street photography - the raw energy of a packed corner, the stark geometry of a dead-end street, and everything candid in between. Total prize pool $3,000: 1st prize $1,500, 2nd $500, 3rd $300, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Judge: Vineet Vohra, the Delhi-based street photographer who became the first Indian Leica Ambassador in 2015 and published his monograph Serendipity in 2024. Winners and finalists have their work professionally printed and presented at TIP's annual group show in London, and are featured to the platform's 985k+ Instagram and 200k+ Facebook following; every entrant receives a free online portfolio permanently hosted on the platform, and photographers retain full copyright in their own work. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3 and $45 for 6, the larger bundles saving 33% and 50% against single entries. AI-generated images are not accepted - submissions must be photography-based, with film, digital, smartphone, tintype and camera-less processes all welcome, and all post-production allowed provided the final result remains photography-based. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px on one side, maximum 10MB per image, and there is no age limit on when the pictures were taken. Competition entry is open to individuals who are at least 18 years old on the date of entry. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $15–$45. Prize: $3,000 pool.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals · Washington Pavilion Visual Arts Center
item.description: The Visual Arts Center at the Washington Pavilion is South Dakota's largest art museum, accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, with eight galleries in downtown Sioux Falls. Its Exhibition Selection Committee keeps a standing, no-deadline route into that programme: proposals are welcome from individual artists, artist groups and guest curators working in any medium or subject matter, and are reviewed on a quarterly basis, with the centre warning that it may take some time for a submission to be scheduled for review. The gallery list is worth reading before proposing - Gallery 301, at the entrance, frequently features photography exhibitions; the 5,000 sq ft Everist Gallery shows work in all media from established regional to international artists; the 1,700 sq ft Jerstad Gallery shows leading regional, national and international artists; the 400 sq ft Shultz Gallery is reserved for emerging regional artists; and the Contemporary Gallery covers digital, installation and new media. Applications go by email and consist of a cover letter summarising your artistic interests with a clear statement of exhibition intention and the galleries you would prioritise, a CV, an artist biography, an artist statement about the proposed body of work, and 10 to 20 high-resolution images at 300 dpi with identifying information for each. No fee is stated anywhere in the guidelines. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ARCHITECTURE · New York Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: NYC4PA's international juried call ARCHITECTURE asks photographers for their vision of the built world - farm houses, split-level ranches and skyscrapers, but equally bridges, private houses, skylines, cathedral interiors, the pyramids of Mexico or the main hall of Grand Central. Whole structures and architectural detail are both welcome, and the organiser is explicit that a building need not be world famous. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers working in any medium, style or school of thought - print, image transfer, emulsion transfer, encaustic, black and white - with experimental and mixed techniques welcome; only 2-D work is eligible and jurying is blind, so no signatures or watermarks on images and no artist names in titles. $4,000 in cash awards go to ten prizewinners: a $1,100 Grand Prize, whose image is featured on the NYC4PA home page, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325 and three Third Prizes of $250, alongside 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions, all included in the NYC4PA online gallery and winners catalog with an award certificate. Images awarded an NYC4PA prize within the past two years are not eligible; images submitted and not selected may be resubmitted at any time. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $40 (first 3 images); $10 each additional. Prize: $1,100 Grand Prize.

item.title: BBA One Shot Award - Autumn 2026
item.description: The Autumn edition of BBA Gallery's single-image photography prize: one photograph, in any photographic medium or genre, from any artist over 18, with no restriction on training or nationality. A shortlist of 20 images is professionally printed and hung at BBA Gallery in Berlin with all production costs covered by the gallery and no shipping cost to the photographer, while a longlist of 50 is shown on a large digital display in the same space. The exhibition falls in the last week of October and is a full-space joint show combining the winning entries of the Summer and Autumn editions. First prize is €300 in cash alongside the exhibition, an Artsy profile and promotion across BBA's social channels and newsletter. Entry is a single JPG, PNG or HEIC file up to 3MB - the low ceiling is for jury review only, with a print-ready file requested if you are shortlisted - and further images can be added by buying extra credits inside the BBA app. Photographers retain full copyright; selected work must be available exclusively for sale through the gallery for the run of the show and three months after, on a 50/50 commission split. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: €19. Prize: €300.

item.title: 64th Annual Juried Competition · Masur Museum of Art
item.description: The Masur Museum of Art in Monroe, Louisiana has run its Annual Juried Competition since 1963, when Ida Kohlmeyer - a student of Mark Rothko - took first place and the museum bought her painting Immanence. It is the museum's longest-running tradition, and a significant share of its 500-work permanent collection, which also holds Picasso, Renoir and Rodin, has been acquired directly through it. The 64th edition is open to artists over 18 living in the United States and working in any medium, with no set theme; the museum receives 1,000-1,500 entries a year and hangs the selection for four months in its historic Main House. Awards total $3,200, with $1,000 for Best in Show, handed out at the March 11 opening reception, plus a separate $100 Best Packed award for the artist who crates their work most professionally - packing peanuts are grounds for disqualification. Accepted work may be offered for sale and the museum takes no commission on those sales. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 85 by 60 inches, three-dimensional work 84 inches tall within a 40 by 40 inch footprint and 200 pounds, and video is capped at five minutes. Entry is $10 per artwork with a minimum of two and a maximum of five, so $20 to $50, and the prospectus asks for recent work (it gives two different completion cutoffs, December 31 2023 in one place and December 31 2024 in another, so confirm with the museum). Submissions open on CaFE on October 1, 2026. This year's juror is not yet named. Artists are notified January 14, 2027, work is delivered February 22 - March 4, and the exhibition runs March 11 - May 15, 2027. One caution on timing: the prospectus gives the deadline as 11:59pm on December 16, but the CaFE portal's own closing field is set a day earlier, so treat December 15 as the safe date to submit by. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: $20–$50. Prize: $3,200 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 US Native American and Indigenous Artists Purchase Initiative · New Mexico Arts
item.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme buys artwork outright for publicly accessible buildings across the state - community centres, courthouses, libraries, healthcare facilities, chapter houses, tribal administrative offices, rest areas and senior centres among them. Of the programme's purchase initiatives this is the one open nationally, rather than to New Mexico residents only or to the six-state Southwest: the goal is to diversify the state collection by buying work from artists at every career stage, and although anyone resident in the United States may apply, special consideration goes to artists who identify as members of a Native American tribe or community. Galleries may submit on behalf of a represented artist regardless of that artist's residency, so long as the artist so identifies. All visual arts media in all genres are considered, and the programme's own artist FAQ names photography explicitly alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, textile, glass, collage and the rest; work must be durable, permanent, low-maintenance and ADA-compliant once installed, and suitable for interior or exterior display. Artists submit an artist statement and up to three images of completed work currently available for purchase, priced between $5,000 and $50,000. That price is all-inclusive - it must cover materials, labour, museum-quality framing under Plexiglas, security hangers, delivery, installation, insurance, taxes, commissions, the project plaque and written and photographic documentation - so budget accordingly. There is no entry fee. Since 1986 AIPP has placed more than 3,000 works across all 33 New Mexico counties, over $21 million paid directly to artists. Finalists are notified in November 2026; purchases are then made on a rolling basis through November 2028, and inclusion in the finalist pool does not guarantee a sale. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$50,000 purchase.

item.title: OPEN ECO 2026 · Photo Fringe
item.description: Photo Fringe is a volunteer-led Brighton charity (registered no. 1148109) that has run an open-platform photography festival since 2003. OPEN ECO 2026 is an exhibition opportunity at Seafront Gallery, Brighton, on view 21 September to 12 October 2026. The organiser's call page is four lines long - venue, run dates, an 11.59pm Tuesday 15 September deadline and a link to the application form - and publishes no fee, no image count, no jury and no theme statement; the Google form needs a sign-in to open, so the 2026 brief and entry terms are visible only to applicants. This is the third edition of the series: the first OPEN Eco showed on Worthing seafront from 2022, and for 2024 Photo Fringe invited anyone who considers themselves a photographer or lens-based artist, worldwide, to answer "How can photography make a difference to the climate crisis?" with a single image, selecting twenty by jury for an outdoor exhibition on Brighton seafront at 10 pounds per entry. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Rolling Submissions: Solo Exhibitions · Ninety-Seven Modern
item.description: Ninety-Seven Modern is an online contemporary gallery founded in Detroit in 2025 by Sierra R. Aguilar, on the premise that the art world is needlessly difficult and exclusive to break into. Its exhibitions are, for now, entirely virtual, which lets viewers anywhere see work by emerging artists, and they rotate on a schedule covering all mediums, processes and origins; the gallery's group shows and its own shop have leaned photographic. Alongside those themed shows it takes rolling proposals for online solo exhibitions, open to "all artists of emerging status, of any age, race, denomination, and demographic". A proposal is up to fifteen high-quality images with title, year, medium and place of creation, a third-person bio attached as a PDF, an artist statement about the work, and your preferred artist name plus any social media and website links, all sent by email with "Solo Exhibition" in the subject line. Selected artists are featured on the gallery site and across its social media. There is no deadline - applications are open on a rolling basis - and the $25 non-refundable application fee is paid through the gallery's own Squarespace shop rather than on the call page. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $25. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Local Lens: Analog Photography Showcase · Kimbell Art Museum
item.description: Open-house showcase in the Kimbell's Piano Pavilion lobby, presented with Courtesy of cofounders Katherine Stephens and Jesse Jackson IV as a Second Saturday event alongside the exhibition Photography's First Century: Masterworks from the Bibliotheque nationale de France. Six photographers working in analog and traditional processes - film, wet plate, cyanotype and other historic techniques - are selected to display finished work together with the negatives, plates, equipment and other artifacts of their process on a 72 x 30 in. table, and to talk with museum visitors about their methods. Each selected artist receives a $150 honorarium. Open to amateurs and professionals at all levels; artists need not be based in the DFW area but must attend the showcase in person on Saturday, December 12, 2026, noon-3 pm. Fully digital photographs and AI-generated images are not permitted. Free to apply: a form plus 3-5 images emailed to the education team. Not a commercial event - no sales are permitted, though artists may share contact information with visitors. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $150 honorarium.

item.title: R.E.D. · Hera Gallery
item.description: Hera Gallery - one of the first women's art cooperatives in the United States, artist-run in Wakefield, Rhode Island since 1974 - is looking for 52 works for its 5th annual international juried virtual exhibition. The brief is the colour and everything it carries: "red lines, red tape, red hats, red flags"; red as aggressive primary, as mysterious, fiery and emotional, as a symbol of passion, war, hate and love - specifically in conversation with current political and cultural states. Open to international artists in all media; because the show is online, high-quality files matter and the gallery warns that poor images will not be reviewed. Three images are required with each entry, but they may be three views of a single artwork rather than three separate pieces. Selected work stays on view at heragallery.org for the whole of 2027, with one artist and work featured across the gallery's social media each week and a virtual artist talk planned for June 2027. Juror Sonja Czekalski is an interdisciplinary artist, Assistant Professor of Art and Art Education Program Coordinator at Central Connecticut State University, an MFA graduate of MassArt and a Hera board member. Hera takes no commission on its juried exhibitions, so 100% of any sale goes to the artist, and it publishes sliding-scale coupon codes for the submission fee on its own calls page. Open call runs September 1 - December 1, 2026. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $35 (sliding scale). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Solo Project Space #9 · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms, the Jersey City gallery run by the non-profit Victory Hall Inc. inside the Topps Building at the Mana Contemporary complex, hands its Project Space and up to four further solo gallery areas to artists with a cohesive body of work or an installation - any theme, any concept, any size or medium. The accepted-media list runs painting or drawing on paper and canvas, collage or textiles, photography, prints and sculpture; work must be original, with no AI and no reproductions. One artist takes the main Project Space and up to four more are given solo areas for the autumn slot, 29 October to 22 November 2026, with an opening reception on Friday 30 October. Installation artists are welcome and are asked to supply a full description of materials and install time. Entry is $35 for up to 15 unframed images at least 1200 pixels on the short side, applicants must be over 18, and all exhibited work must be for sale with 60% of proceeds to the artist. Accepted work is dropped off in Jersey City on 16, 17 or 18 October, or shipped to arrive by Monday 19 October, with shipping arranged directly with the director. Artists selected for any 2026 show get preferred status for the gallery's end-of-year Big Small Show, and may also be picked up for other Drawing Rooms programmes including The Art Project JC lobbies and the gallery's Artsy.net exhibits. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: smallART 2026/27 · Arts Illiana
item.description: Arts Illiana's Terre Haute gallery devotes its winter slot to small-scale work, with nothing larger than 12 by 12 inches framed for two-dimensional pieces or 12 inches cubed for sculpture. Entries must be original work in any art medium, made in the past five years and not previously shown at the gallery; the prospectus names photography outright among the processes it expects artists to describe, citing 'inkjet print of digital photograph on archival paper' and 'dye sublimation print of digital photograph on aluminium' as model entries. There is no entry fee and artists may submit up to five works. A guest curator selects, and cash awards are given in specific categories. The show is open ONLY to artists in Arts Illiana's six-county Indiana region - Clay, Parke, Putnam, Sullivan, Vermillion and Vigo - plus the Illinois counties of Clark and Edgar. Accepted work is delivered 27-31 October and 3-7 November; the exhibition opens with a reception on Friday 13 November 2026 and runs to 6 February 2027. Everything hung must be for sale, with the gallery taking a 30% commission, and framed work must be glazed in acrylic or Plexiglas rather than glass. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: TJAA Rotating Curated Art Exhibition #7
item.description: The Texas Jewish Arts Association hangs the seventh in its rotating series of curated exhibitions at the Dallas Jewish Community Foundation on Merit Drive. There is no theme and no entry fee, and the call is open to all genres, all mediums, all sizes and all styles for both two- and three-dimensional work, so photography is eligible on the organisers' own terms. Members may submit up to five pieces; the curators choose on the basis of what fits and hangs well together in the available space rather than on a competitive jury, and not being selected is explicitly not a judgement on the work. The Foundation offers a $180 Visitor Choice Award. Entry is a membership benefit, so a current TJAA membership is required - membership is open to all, costs $18 a year for students up to 26 and $36 for adults, and TJAA offers a no-questions-asked complimentary membership to anyone who cannot afford the dues; new members joining before the deadline are welcome. All work must arrive gallery-ready with D-rings and wire, and accepted pieces must be delivered in person in Dallas on Thursday 17 September, with the shipping address listed only as 'to be determined'. The exhibition opens on Monday 21 September and closes 22 October 2026, with collection on 25 October and a $10-a-day storage charge after that. Sales are handled directly between artist and buyer, with TJAA requesting a 20% donation that funds cash awards at its future shows. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: Free (TJAA membership from $18/year). Prize: $180 Visitor Choice Award + Exhibition.

item.title: Postmark Arts & Cultural Programming Grant 2027 · City of Auburn Parks, Arts & Recreation
item.description: The City of Auburn and the Auburn Arts Commission fund arts and cultural programming at the Postmark Center for the Arts, the city's arts venue at 20 Auburn Avenue, and at the adjoining outdoor Auburn Arts Alley. Grants of $500 to $2,000 go to the strongest proposals for programmes that take place there during 2027 and are free to the public - exhibitions, screenings, workshops, readings, performances and celebrations are all named as qualifying public benefit, so a photography show, a documentary screening or a darkroom workshop all fit. Individuals, community groups and arts organisations may apply and 501(c)(3) status is not required; no residency restriction is stated, but the programme must happen at the Postmark Center, and projects that charge admission, serve mainly an organisation's own membership, support religious activities or political organisations, or fund scholarships and ticket subsidies are excluded. The flexible-use hall seats about 90 theatre-style, with two glass-walled meeting rooms alongside. Applications are scored on artistic quality, community impact and accessibility, planning and capacity to deliver; the granting committee meets in November 2026 and payment is made on completion, against an invoice and final report. There is no application fee. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500–$2,000.

item.title: Earth Matters · Atlantic Gallery
item.description: Earth Matters is the annual juried open call from Atlantic Gallery, the artist-run cooperative that has operated in New York's Chelsea gallery district since 1974. It invites artists whose work is earth-made as well as those whose practice is earth-focused, exploring our relationship to land and water, geology and ecology, and the interconnected environments that sustain all life - work the gallery describes as residing in the sublime, spiritual, geological, topographical, ecological, biophilic, scientific, cultural, social and sustainable realms, whether non-objective or carrying a deeper message, materially driven or conceptually based. Artists employing earth-derived materials and those exploring earth matter through image, process, research, environmental inquiry or metaphor are equally encouraged to apply. The juror is Judith Kruger, a multidisciplinary American artist recognised internationally for her advocacy and use of historic natural pigments and ecological processes, whose work is held by the Mattatuck Museum, the Hammond Museum, Savannah College of Art and Design and Wofford College, and who also jurored Atlantic Gallery's 2020 juried exhibition. Photography is named in the accepted-media list alongside oils, acrylics, watercolours, pastels, drawings, prints, mixed media and sculpture in any medium; digital and giclee reproductions of original artwork and AI-generated work are excluded. Entry is open to international and US artists 18 and over at $35 for up to three works plus $10 for up to five more submitted at the same time, with no piece exceeding 36 inches wide by 40 inches high and all work made within the last five years. Selected work is shown at the gallery from 16 February to 6 March 2027, and award winners are chosen for inclusion in a later Atlantic Gallery group show in Chelsea. All work must be for sale, and the gallery takes 40% commission. Accepted work has to be delivered to the Chelsea gallery in person or by proxy during regular gallery hours - no shipping option is offered and the gallery disclaims liability for work in transit - so artists applying from outside New York should plan for that before paying the fee. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images), $10 for 5 more. Prize: Group exhibition in Chelsea, NYC.

item.title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #140 — Portfolio 2026
item.description: A portfolio issue of F-Stop Magazine, the online photography magazine publishing themed issues since 2004. Issue #140 asks for a single project or body of work rather than a loose group of pictures: 12 to 20 photographs plus a project statement, which is required for Portfolio issues. One submission per person per issue, entry is free and there is no payment for images that are included. Submissions go by email; selected work is published on the magazine's site and stays in the archive indefinitely. Publication is expected around December 1, 2026. — Deadline: November 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Paris International Street Photo Awards 2026
item.description: An annual street photography award run from Paris, open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide aged 18 or over. Entries are made as single images or as series of 5 to 15 photographs, judged separately in each of about forty street-photography categories — from classic street and black & white to urbex, night shots, film photography and street humour. Street Photographer of the Year takes $1,000, Best Street Photo Project $700 and Street Photo of the Year $500, all paid by PayPal. Winners, jury nominees and finalists are exhibited at the organisers' expense — the 2026 edition will be shown at an international photo festival in New York in late 2027 — and grand-prize winners get a monograph published with partner Snap Collective plus features in FotoSlovo and OPENEYE magazines. Entry is €18 for a single image up to September 30 and €21 from October 1, with series and multi-image packages priced up to €75; each additional category costs €6. Photographers keep copyright; previously published and previously entered work is accepted. Winners are announced December 26, 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: €18–€75 (+€6 per extra category). Prize: $1,000 / $700 / $500 + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: In and Out of Balance · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms, the Jersey City gallery run by the non-profit Victory Hall Inc. inside the Topps Building at the Mana Contemporary complex, invites work for a group show about visual weight, tension and spatial harmony. The gallery asks how balance is managed inside a picture: symmetrical arrangements that read as calm and ordered, asymmetrical ones where unequal elements hold equal visual weight through colour, size and negative space, compositions that radiate from a central axis, and deliberate weight shifts that make a work feel precarious. Its own reference list runs from Richard Serra and Malevich to Agnes Martin, Sarah Sze, Wangechi Mutu and Cecily Brown. Acceptable media are named as painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, photography, sculpture or any other fine art medium, and work must be original - the gallery accepts no AI and no reproductions. Anne Trauben, the gallery's curator and director, selects. Entry is $35 for up to three images, jpegs at least 1200 pixels on any side, and applicants must be over 18. The exhibition runs 29 October to 21 November 2026 with an opening reception on 30 October, Meet the Artists on 8 November and a closing reception on 22 November. Sales split 60% to the artist and 40% to the gallery, and artists chosen here are also considered for the gallery's other programmes, including the Art Project JC lobbies and its Artsy exhibitions. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 46th Annual Western Spirit Juried Art Show & Sale · Cheyenne Frontier Days Old West Museum
item.description: The Cheyenne Frontier Days Old West Museum runs one of the Rocky Mountain region's larger juried shows, and photography sits in it as a full medium with its own Best of Media award rather than as an afterthought: the 2026 edition hung more than 240 works by over 100 artists across acrylic, drawing, mixed media, oil, pastel, photography, printmaking, sculpture and watercolour, with a sponsored Best Photography award among the prizes. The show wants original work interpreting the American West, and the prospectus draws a firm line around the photography category - images should represent reality with only minor adjustments, meaning exposure, colour correction, cropping and light retouching, and anything edited further has to be entered as mixed media. For the 46th edition an independent jury of professionals from the Western art community selects the show, which runs 6 March to 18 April 2027. Awards are $1,000 Best of Show, $500 Best of Each Media, $250 Best Student Artist and $100 Best Miniature, and there is a separate student category. Entry is $20 per work for non-members and $10 for members, up to four works; the member rate needs a discount code from the museum before you submit. Entries opened on 1 September 2026 and close on 14 November, with acceptances announced 11 December - the prospectus contradicts itself on that date, its calendar giving 14 November and a line on page two saying 2 November, so enter early. Work must be original, made in the last three years and not previously shown for sale at the museum, with 2-D limited to 47 by 60 inches including frame. Everything accepted must be for sale for the run of the show and the museum takes 35% commission, which also applies to work sold within 30 days of closing. AI-generated artwork and installation art are not eligible. — Deadline: November 14, 2026. Fee: $20 per entry ($10 members). Prize: $1,000 Best of Show + $500 Best of Each Media.

item.title: Close to Home · Loft Artists Association
item.description: The Loft Artists Association, founded in 1978 by three artists who took studios in a vacant lock factory and now settled into two galleries and fourteen studios at 575 Pacific Street in Stamford, Connecticut, opens its autumn juried exhibition to all artists. Home, the gallery says, can be a place, a person, a memory, a community or simply a feeling, and artists are invited to consider what feels familiar, intimate or deeply known and what happens when you look at it again. Variations in size and shape are encouraged and both two- and three-dimensional work is wanted; the entry rules state plainly that all mediums are acceptable, so lens-based work is eligible on the same terms as everything else. Anna Patalano juries, and there are cash awards for Best in Show and first, second and third runner-up. Entry is $30 for the first work and $15 for each additional, up to five, and multiple entries must be submitted together on EntryThingy to get the discount. Wall work may be up to 60 inches wide and 72 inches high before framing and sculpture up to six feet. Notification is 26 October, delivery 1 and 2 November, and the show runs 7 November to 20 December 2026 with an opening reception on 7 November. Work for sale is encouraged and the association takes 20% commission. Past juried shows here have drawn over 300 entries from more than 120 artists. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: $30 first work + $15 each additional. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 39th Annual Members Only Show · Texas Photographic Society
item.description: Texas Photographic Society's 39th annual members show, juried by Amy Holmes George, a fine art photographer, Fulbright Scholar and former TPS executive director whose own work moves between traditional photography, digital imaging, alternative processes and mixed media. The call is open themed and welcomes photographers of all levels internationally who are at least 18; all photography-based work is encouraged, including digital, silver and alternative processes. Selected work is exhibited at the Center for Contemporary Arts in Abilene, Texas, opening November 13 2026 and running to a closing reception on January 15 2027, with prints due at the gallery by November 6 and local drop-off available November 2 to 6. Awards are $400 for first place, $250 for second, $150 for third and up to five honorable mentions; TPS board members may enter but cannot win. Entry is $30 for five images plus $5 for each additional image, up to twelve, and you must be a current TPS member, though you can join or renew inside the CaFE application at the time of entry (memberships start at $20 student and military, $40 individual). Work previously shown in a TPS exhibition is not eligible, and TPS takes no commission on prints sold during the show. One caution on timing: TPS states the deadline as 11:59pm Mountain on Friday 2 October, but the CaFE portal's own closing field is set a day earlier, so treat 1 October as the safe date to submit by. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $30 / 5 images + $5 each (membership from $20). Prize: $400 / $250 / $150.

item.title: The Sacred Ordinary · Mercury 20 Gallery
item.description: Mercury 20 Gallery, an artist-run contemporary gallery founded in Oakland in 2006 and operated by San Francisco Bay Area artists, is seeking work for its annual juried group exhibition on the theme The Sacred Ordinary. The call invites artists to explore the beauty, meaning and quiet significance found in everyday life, considering how the mundane, domestic, familiar or overlooked can be elevated into something sacred or extraordinary through personal experience, memory, ritual, observation or transformation. Artists are encouraged to interpret the theme broadly and in their own distinctive ways, using a variety of artistic mediums including painting, sculpture, collage, photography and mixed media; all 2D and 3D media are accepted except video and performance. The juror is Svea Lin Soll, a curator and art consultant with nearly 30 years of experience across galleries, museums and independent practice, who has curated over 70 exhibitions and is co-curating Kōmij Mour Ijin / Our Life Is Here, a two-year project with UC Berkeley and the David Brower Center. One artist in any medium will be selected for a solo exhibition in the gallery's Back Room in 2027. The show runs 8 January to 6 February 2027 at 475 25th Street with an opening reception on 9 January. Entry is open to emerging and established artists 18 and over who can hand deliver and collect their work, as nothing can be shipped or stored; work must be original and completed within the last three years, no more than 60 inches in any direction or 25 lb, and the gallery holds 50% commission on sales. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35/3 works + $10 each addl (max 5). Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Artist Residency at MCCC · Mercer County Community College
item.description: The Gallery at Mercer County Community College runs a bi-annual residency programme for artists working in any medium, and is now taking proposals for the Spring 2027 semester. Four residencies are awarded, each three weeks long, in two terms: Term A from 25 January to 12 February and Term B from 22 February to 12 March 2027. Two residencies are designated for Mercer County artists and two for artists living outside the county, so the call is genuinely open beyond the region. Each resident is assigned one of the Gallery's two side spaces to make an exhibition or performance-based project and shows alongside another resident working in the mirroring space. Residents are required to collaborate with MCCC students and staff on their project and to run workshops in the main gallery, and the Gallery says it especially values projects that prioritise student engagement; faculty add their own talks and events around the project spaces. The Gallery welcomes proposals in all media, including but not limited to painting, sculpture, installation, performance, photography and video. A $350 stipend is paid on successful completion. Practical limits are stated plainly: the side spaces are designed for exhibitions rather than studios and facilities are limited, artists transport their own work and materials, the Gallery covers no shipping or travel costs, work can only be done during gallery open hours, and the space must be returned to its original condition. The Gallery does not handle sales but will pass enquiries to the artist. An application is a portfolio of 5 to 10 images of recent work, a resume with current address, an artist statement and a project proposal specific to the gallery space that sets out the student collaboration and workshops. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $350 stipend + gallery residency.

item.title: 2027 Spring Artist in Residence at Hudson Gardens · South Suburban Public Art Committee
item.description: Presented by the South Suburban Public Art Committee, the Hudson Gardens Artist in Residence programme gives one artist dedicated time and space to work while engaging the public in a garden setting in Littleton, Colorado. The artist works in the Pavilion at Hudson Gardens, a large, light-filled, climate-controlled space with tables, chairs, water and electricity, surrounded by seasonal landscapes, walking paths, wildlife and year-round visitors. This term runs 17 to 22 May 2027. The residency is deliberately public-facing: mornings are closed studio, afternoons are open studio from 1 to 4pm Tuesday to Friday, and Saturday runs 11am to 5pm including the closing reception, so applicants should be comfortable making work while visitors watch and ask questions. The resident develops and presents at least one public engagement activity - a workshop, demonstration, artist talk or interactive experience - with up to $200 of participant materials covered, and a residency coordinator supports setup, logistics and programming. A $1,100 stipend is paid on successful completion; lodging and transport are not provided. The call is open to artists working in all visual art mediums and disciplines, aged 18 and over, individuals only - teams, collectives, organisations and commercial entities are not eligible - and artists from Colorado and beyond are encouraged to apply. The Pavilion is not suited to large-scale fabrication, heavy machinery, extensive ventilation, significant dust, hazardous materials, open flames or specialised industrial equipment; hand-built small-scale ceramics are possible with off-site firing. An application is an artist statement, a residency proposal with goals, a description of the proposed public engagement activity, a CV and 8 to 12 images of work completed in the last five years. Selection is on artistic merit, fit with the garden setting, the quality and accessibility of the proposed public programme, and feasibility. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,100 stipend.

item.title: Fall Show Open Call · Upside Down LA
item.description: Upside Down is a donation-based coffee, art and community space in Westwood Village serving the neighbourhood and UCLA, open since 2019 and owned and operated by Jews for Jesus, with a gallery that has staged more than twenty exhibitions since 2019. For its fall show it is looking for local Los Angeles artists with pieces, new or old, that explore the concept of lingering. Suggested threads include staying, stopping, remaining, holding back, pausing, rest before movement, the end of the celebration, silence, calm after the climax, home, consideration of place, presence, retention, leftovers and assemblage. The organisers frame the theme around Shemini Atzeret, the eighth day of assembly, which falls outside the usual seven-day cycle and reads as an extra day to gather before separating, and they ask what it looks like to recognise the sacredness of a moment even as it passes, to stay after the party is over, to reflect before rushing on. All mediums are accepted, including visual arts, poetry and music, and up to three pieces may be submitted. There is no entry fee. Accepted work is shown in the fall exhibition, which runs 17 October to 4 December 2026 with an opening reception; selected artists can exhibit and sell their work and take part in exhibition-related events. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Permanent Open Call · The Slow Archive
item.description: A rolling, no-deadline call from The Slow Archive, an independent platform for slow landscape photography whose debut digital volume, Traces, came out of its 2026 open call. The archive says it remains perpetually open to new perspectives through an ongoing submission process, and invites landscape photography projects that delve into the quiet nuances of slow time, memory, subtle traces and the poetic nature of peripheral spaces. Both a fully realised series and an evocative long-term work in progress are welcome; the editors say they are looking for a contemplative gaze rather than a finished statement. Photographers submit portfolios for rolling review and potential publication, and the archive also uses the call to find fresh viewpoints for its digital platforms and social feed. Selected contributions are curated for the online journal and may be considered for future printed volumes or physical exhibitions. Free to enter through a Google Form, with no closing date, so a project can be sent whenever it is ready. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Winter 2026 Residency · SITE Toronto
item.description: Two three-month residencies at SITE Toronto, a non-profit launched in January 2026 with a crowdfunding campaign and built around funded time rather than exhibition deadlines. One place goes to a Toronto-based artist or curator, who receives funding to travel abroad for research or professional development; the other goes to a resident from elsewhere, who is flown to Toronto and housed in a private apartment for the full term. Both receive a CAD $3,000 stipend, up to CAD $1,500 in travel support, a private studio, one-to-one mentorship with an artist, curator or other cultural practitioner of their own choosing, the chance to produce a SITE Edition and to conceive a public programme, and access to SITE's network. The Toronto place is delivered with XinResidence and prioritises practitioners at a formative stage and from communities that have historically faced barriers to space, resources and institutional support. Photographers are squarely in scope: Spring 2026 resident Yantong Li made a photographic edition out of the residency, an archival print on Hahnemuhle photo rag, with Beichen Zhang. The session runs November 16, 2026 to February 19, 2027. Applications are free and go through a Google Form linked from the residencies page; the deadline is noon EST on Monday September 14, and shortlisted applicants may be invited to an online interview the week of September 21. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000 CAD stipend + Residency.

item.title: Camargo Fellowship 2027-2028
item.description: Ten-week research residencies at the Camargo Foundation in Cassis, on the Mediterranean coast near Marseille, founded in 1971 by the American artist and philanthropist Jerome Hill and with more than 1,500 fellows behind it. Fourteen fellowships are awarded a year, seven to artists and seven to scholars and thinkers, across two sessions: 8 September to 17 November 2027 and 23 February to 4 May 2028. Each fellow gets a furnished apartment on the campus, a €350 weekly stipend (€3,500 over the ten weeks) and basic return travel to Cassis; the campus holds twelve apartments, a reference library, an open-air theatre and one artist's studio with a darkroom, though the Foundation supplies no art materials or technical equipment. Artists choose one of six subcategories, among them Visual Artists and Film, Video and Digital Artists, and must have maintained a professional practice for at least five years with a track record of exhibitions, publications, credits, awards or grants - the Foundation is looking for a fully developed, mature voice, not an emerging one. Teams of up to three may apply jointly, with a stipend and travel grant for each member. Applications are free and submitted in English through Submittable; supporting material may be in English or French, and an international panel of independent jurors selects. Every fellow leads one resident session for the group during the stay, and attendance at the others' is required. The Foundation has said this is the last edition to run as a public open call before the selection process changes in July 2027. Both the guidelines PDF and the Submittable portal close the window on 1 October 2026, 23:59 CET; a summary line on the Foundation's own apply page says the call runs to 30 September, so do not leave it to the last day. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,500 stipend + Residency.

item.title: FFYNNU Celf Artist Residency · Plas Glyn-y-Weddw
item.description: Open to artists living and working in Wales only. Four paid residencies at Plas Glyn-y-Weddw, an arts centre and accredited museum in Llanbedrog on the Llyn Peninsula in north Wales, run in partnership with the community climate movement GwyrddNi and funded by Arts Council of Wales, GwyrddNi, Adra and the John Andrews Trust. Two of the four places are reserved for artists based in north Wales (Ynys Mon, Gwynedd, Conwy, Denbighshire, Flintshire and Wrexham). It is aimed at artists whose practice already connects with environmental, ecological or climate subjects, and it is open across visual art forms. Each residency runs 14 flexible days between October 2026 and early March 2027 and pays a £3,500 artist fee (£250 a day) plus £500 for materials and kit, £35 a day subsistence, up to £500 of travel, free on-site accommodation and a workspace, along with two days of mentoring with an industry specialist and two further paid networking days with the other residents. The emphasis is on research and experimentation rather than finished work - there is no expectation to produce a resolved piece - and each residency ends in a sharing of the artist's own choosing and scale. Applicants must be over 18, able to demonstrate two years of committed practice, and not currently studying in higher education. Answers to the application questions may be given in writing, audio or video; an Access Fund, staff-assisted application sessions and a Disability Arts Cymru officer on the selection panel are all built in, though the current on-site accommodation is not wheelchair accessible. Free to apply, and the deadline is 11pm on Friday 4 September 2026, with shortlisting and interviews in mid-to-late September. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £3,500 artist fee + Residency.

item.title: Gender Equality Grant · Pulitzer Center
item.description: A rolling, themed reporting grant from the Pulitzer Center for investigative, data-driven projects on gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls. Open worldwide to freelance journalists, staff journalists and groups of newsrooms collaborating on a project idea, with the Center saying it strongly encourages proposals from journalists and newsrooms representing a broad array of social, racial, ethnic and economic backgrounds and underrepresented groups, and that it aims to support teams that reflect the communities they report on. There is no budget range and no cap on the number of projects funded in a year; the average Pulitzer Center grant is about $5,000. The grant will not cover staff salaries, equipment purchases, books, feature-length films, an outlet's general expenses or seed money, but contractor costs such as data researchers, illustrators or data-visualisation and story designers can go in the budget, and short documentaries with an ambitious distribution plan are supported. An application is a 250-word project description, a preliminary budget with a basic breakdown of costs, and a distribution plan; proposals are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed as they arrive, with applicants typically told within a month whether they are being considered, and any urgency in the field reporting should be stated in the application. Photographers are well represented among the work the Center points to as examples: Women on the Move by The Everyday Projects, Anita Pouchard Serra on immigrant women in Buenos Aires, and Neha Wadekar and Will Swanson on climate-driven early marriage in northern Kenya. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 average grant.

item.title: Members Only 2026 · K Space Contemporary
item.description: Juried, non-thematic exhibition of new work by members of K Space Contemporary, the 501(c)(3) contemporary art space in downtown Corpus Christi. Held only in even-numbered years, it exists to put a member's work in front of a panel of Coastal Bend art professionals: the Best of Show winner is awarded a solo exhibition at K Space in 2027 or 2028, with cash awards for second and third place. All visual art media are accepted, including photography - the gallery bars only reproductions such as giclee or inkjet copies of original works, and video is exhibited on a 58-inch screen. Each artist may submit one or two works completed in the last two years and not previously shown at K Space; 40 to 50 top-scoring works are hung. Two-dimensional work must be no wider than 60 inches and wired to hang, with Plexi rather than glass. Entry is $10 plus K Space membership, which can be bought inside the entry system ($20 student or senior 65+, $35 individual). All work must be for sale, with a 40% gallery commission. Notification November 12; the show runs November 28, 2026 to January 22, 2027, with an ArtWalk reception and awards on December 4. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $10 + membership ($20-$35). Prize: Solo exhibition + cash awards.

item.title: 2026 New Exhibiting Members · Buffalo Society of Artists
item.description: Annual jury for exhibiting membership of the Buffalo Society of Artists, founded in 1891 and one of the oldest artist societies in the United States. Exhibiting membership is the gate to the Society's juried programme - the annual Catalogue Exhibition, the Open Members show, the Summer and Thumb Box exhibitions - and its 226 current exhibiting members include working photographers, so a photographic practice is judged on the same footing as painting or printmaking. Applicants upload a resume, a brief artist statement and 9 to 13 works made in the last three years; video artists submit a single MP4 of up to ten minutes instead. Three of the uploaded works must then be brought as originals to an in-person review on Saturday, October 10 at Our Lady of Hope Parish in Buffalo, drop-off 9:30-10:15am and pick-up by 1pm. The seven-member review panel is named in advance and includes two photographers - Christina Buscarino, gallerist of the C. Stuart and Jane H. Hunt Art Gallery, and Nate Ely, education director at CEPA - alongside Hallwalls deputy director Parrish Gibbons; it scores each applicant on artist statement, innovation, technical facility, presentation and exhibition history. Open to artists 18 or over who currently live in Western New York and are not enrolled in an undergraduate visual arts degree. The $25 jurying fee is non-refundable, the application window runs September 1 to midnight on October 2, 2026, decisions are sent by mail by October 17, and accepted artists then pay $50 annual dues. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Exhibition membership.

item.title: Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships 2027
item.description: Annual fellowship programme from Vital Impacts, the 501(c)(3) co-founded by photographer Ami Vitale, supporting visual storytellers working on long-term documentary projects about environmental and conservation issues. For 2027 the foundation awards one $20,000 fellowship to an established environmental photographer, named for Dr. Jane Goodall, six $5,000 fellowships to emerging photographers, and ten places on an intensive mentorship programme; one fellow is also invited to exhibit at the 2027 Festival of Ethical Photography in Lodi, Italy. Recipients have twelve months to develop their project with publishing and showcase support from Vital Impacts. The foundation strongly favours photographers with a meaningful, sustained relationship to the community, place or issue they propose to document, and is drawn to work that moves past documenting environmental problems to the people and initiatives working toward solutions. You do not have to live permanently in a place to qualify - recurring travel, long-term collaboration or professional and academic engagement also count. Prior publication experience is not required, and applicants may write in their native language, with translation arranged. Submit 20 images from one or two bodies of work plus a synopsis, project statement and biography. Applications open August 31, 2026 on Picter; the $25 fee is waived for applicants from developing countries and on request for economic hardship. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $25 (waivers available). Prize: $20,000 + 6 × $5,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: We: Culture · CICA Museum
item.description: International group exhibition at CICA Museum in Gimpo, South Korea, gathering work on culture in its many registers - multiculturalism, identity, subcultures, social media culture, pop culture, and ideas of nation, religion and race. Photography is named first among the welcomed media and "Photographs & 2D Digital Art" is one of four submission categories alongside video and interactive art, physical works, and performance. Submission is free and by email: up to five JPEGs and/or three links to video works, plus a bio. Selected photographic and digital work is printed at 10x15 or 10x10 inches, framed and installed by the museum's team; artists sending physical work ship at their own cost, with 2D pieces capped at 39 inches on the longest side and wall-mounted work at 10 kg. Accepted artists contribute $78 USD (110,000 KRW) per piece toward exhibition processing and maintenance. The show runs April 28 - May 16, 2027, and the museum notes the dates are subject to change. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $78 per accepted work. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: After Love: Broken Hearts & Broken Bodies · OVADA
item.description: Group exhibition at OVADA's warehouse gallery in central Oxford inviting artists to respond to romantic heartbreak, relationship breakdown and the strategies we use to survive love's endings. The show is part of a four-century historical study of heartbreak as an embodied emotion by Dr Sally Holloway, funded by an Arts & Humanities Research Council fellowship, with partners including Oxfordshire Mind and the Poetry Pharmacy. OVADA calls it a radically inclusive exhibition where all eligible works will be shown - there is no jury - and the hang is arranged salon style by Audrey Baldwin and Sally Holloway as work arrives on install day. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, collage, textiles, printmaking, ceramics, sculpture and video; work must be wall-hung or free-standing and no larger than 2m x 2m. Up to three works per artist. Open to artists 18 and over resident in the UK; work must be delivered in person on Saturday 3 October and collected on 18 or 19 October, as the gallery cannot accept posted submissions. Images of exhibited work also appear in an ArtSteps digital version of the show. The exhibition runs 7-18 October 2026, with a launch on the evening of 7 October. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: £10 (1 work), £15 (2 works), £20 (3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: In the Moment · PhotoMidwest
item.description: Members' exhibition mounted as part of PhotoMidwest's 2026 Biennial Festival, shown at the University of Wisconsin's Pyle Center in Madison and in the organisation's online gallery. Each PhotoMidwest member may enter one image, free of charge, on any subject - the show is framed around photography's ability to make a moment permanent, whether it documents a slice of reality or a vision from the artist's imagination. There is no jury: the Pyle Center has wall space for up to 80 framed pieces according to the call page, or up to 75 according to the entry form, and if more entries arrive than there is wall they are hung in the order they were entered, first come first served. Every entry appears in the online gallery regardless, and members who would rather not frame can enter for the online gallery only. Framed work is capped at 30 inches on the longest dimension; files should be 2000-2500 pixels on the long edge, sRGB, under 2.5 MB, with no watermarks or borders. The exhibition runs November 2, 2026 - January 29, 2027. Entry requires PhotoMidwest membership. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: IMPRINT · The Hook Experiment
item.description: A juried international group exhibition about the impressions that shape us — the visible and invisible traces of memory, identity, history and human experience, and the stories we inherit, rewrite or leave behind. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, assemblage, wood, glass, ceramics and collage; video, electronics and anything needing power are excluded, and every finished work must measure exactly 10 x 10 inches. The Hook Experiment is a 4,500-square-foot gallery and creative space in a partially renovated building on Oxford, Pennsylvania's main street, founded to give artists room for risk and imperfection outside commercial pressure. Selected work hangs November 20, 2026 – January 16, 2027 with opening and closing receptions plus school and community engagement events; artists keep 70% of sales and may mark work NFS. Artists ship both ways with a prepaid return label or hand-deliver on November 7–8. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $25 (up to 3 works) / $5 each additional, max 6. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: YICCA Prize 26/27
item.description: An international contemporary art prize run since 2010 by the Italian association A.P.S. MOHO, open to artists and groups of any nationality with no qualification requirements; all techniques are accepted, photography included, and works may be up to 3 x 3 metres. A jury selects 18 artists for the final exhibition at the New Art Space, Cannaregio 883, Venice, running November 14–28, 2026, and selected work is published in the YICCA catalogue, distributed free to finalists and to the collectors, press and curators invited to the opening. Cash prizes total €5,500 — €3,000 first, €1,000 second, €500 third and a €1,000 prize reserved for students — paid by the main sponsor by bank transfer, and scored one third each by the jury, the association and the host gallery. The jury roster is due to be published before the entry deadline. Artists carry shipping and any insurance on exhibited work. — Deadline: October 8, 2026. Fee: €55 (1 work) – €165 (6 works). Prize: €5,500 in cash prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: Visual Languages Across Cultures — ZAO Magazine · Molend Art
item.description: A guest-edited special issue of ZAO, the independent art magazine published in Glasgow by Molend Art and carrying an ISSN assigned through the British Library. The issue asks how contemporary art becomes a shared language across cultures, and looks for work reflecting on cultural diaspora, identity, memory and cross-cultural communication. All mediums are accepted — painting, sculpture, photography, installation, ceramics, mixed media, digital media, performance documentation, textile and experimental practices — from artists 18 and over worldwide at any career stage, up to six original works each. Guest editor Mengyi Grace Wang, a contemporary artist and researcher, works with editor-in-chief Bowen Wu. ZAO favours practices that are still unfolding and builds a cultural passage between East Asia and the UK. Free to enter; AI-generated work is strictly prohibited. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.
